'''Beer soup''' ({{Langx|de|Biersuppe}}, {{langx|gsw-FR|Biersupp}}, {{langx|cs|Pivní polévka}}) is a [[soup]] which is usually [[roux]]-based and made with [[beer]].<ref>{{Cite book | last = Lennert | first = Joachim | title = Culinary guidebook: Germany | publisher = Hueber Verlag | date = 2003 | page = 103 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=TEoZn7kOPf8C&pg=PT99 | isbn = 978-3-19-006382-6}}</ref> In [[Middle Ages|medieval]] Europe, it was served as a breakfast soup,<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=ptZgNoobsyUC&dq=%22beer+soup%22&pg=PA128 1,001 Foods to Die For - Andrews McMeel Publishing, Madison Books - Google Books<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> sometimes poured over bread. A popular variant in [[Wisconsin]] restaurants and bars is called '''beer cheese soup''', made with melted cheese, vegetables, and sometimes incorporating [[bratwurst]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Beer Cheese Soup: A Wisconsin Classic |url=https://www.wisconsincheeseman.com/blog/cooking/beer-cheese-soup-wisconsin-classic/ |website=The Wisconsin Cheeseman}}</ref>

Variations on the recipe use the starchiness of [[potato]] as a thickener.<ref>{{Cite book | last = Alper | first = Nicole |author2=Lynette Rohrer | title = Wild women in the kitchen: 101 rambunctious recipes & 99 tasty tales | publisher = Red Wheel | date = 1996 | page = 23 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=8zKBmkw0kVIC&pg=PA23 | isbn = 978-1-57324-030-7}}</ref> The [[Sorbs|Sorbian]] version is sweet, with cream and raisins added.{{Cn|date=February 2025}}
